questions.text: Two numbers are chosen independently and uniformly at random from the set {1, 2, ..., 13}. The probability (rounded off to 3 decimal places) that their 4-bit (unsigned) binary representations have the same most significant bit is ___________
questions.solution:
In 4 bits, the MSB is 1 for 8-13 (6 numbers) and 0 for 1-7 (7 numbers).

[latex]P=\left(\frac{7}{13}\right)^2+\left(\frac{6}{13}\right)^2=\frac{49+36}{169}=\frac{85}{169}\approx0.503[/latex]

Answer: 0.503

questions.text:
Consider three concurrent processes P1, P2 and P3 as shown below, which access a shared variable D that has been initialized to 100.

The process are executed on a uniprocessor system running a time-shared operating system. If the minimum and maximum possible values of D after the three processes have completed execution are X and Y respectively, then the value of Y-X is __________.
questions.solution:
Each update is really load D, change, store D, so a process can overwrite the others' results.

- Maximum: lose P2's update. P1 reads 100; P2 runs fully (D = 50); P1 writes 120; then P3 makes it 130. So [latex]Y=130[/latex].
- Minimum: lose both additions. P2 reads 100; P1 and P3 run fully (D = 130); P2 writes 100 [latex]-[/latex] 50 = 50. So [latex]X=50[/latex].

[latex]Y-X=130-50=80[/latex]

Answer: 80

questions.text: Consider a sequence of 14 elements: A = [-5, -10, 6, 3, -1, -2, 13, 4, -9, -1, 4, 12, -3, 0]. The sequence sum [latex]S(i,j)=\sum_{k=i}^{j}A[k][/latex]. Determine the maximum of S(i,j), where [latex]0 \leq i \leq j \lt 14[/latex]. (Divide and conquer approach may be used). Answer:______
questions.solution:
Use Kadane's idea (running sum, restart when it goes negative):
[latex]-[/latex]5, [latex]-[/latex]10 are dropped. From 6: running sums 6, 9, 8, 6, 19, 23, 14, 13, 17, 29, 26, 26.

Maximum subarray = 6 + 3 [latex]-[/latex] 1 [latex]-[/latex] 2 + 13 + 4 [latex]-[/latex] 9 [latex]-[/latex] 1 + 4 + 12 = 29.

Answer: 29
